chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah about a man who arrives after the people have departed from Arafat. He said: If he has time to go to Arafat from its night, stand there, then depart and catch the people at al-Mash'ar before they depart, his Hajj is not complete until he goes to Arafat. And if a man arrives and Arafat has been missed for him, let him stand at al-Mash'ar al-Haram, for indeed Allah the Exalted has excused His servant, and his Hajj is complete if he catches al-Mash'ar al-Haram before the sunrise and before the people depart. If he does not catch al-Mash'ar al-Haram, then Hajj has been missed for him, and let him make it a separate Umrah, and upon him is the Hajj next year.

key_terms.الْمَشْعَرِ الْحَرَامِ: Al-Mash'ar al-Haram, the sacred monument (typically Mash'ar al-Haram in Muzdalifah)
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat, the plain where the essential standing (wuquf) of Hajj takes place
key_terms.عُمْرَةً مُفْرَدَةً: A separate Umrah, performed independently when Hajj is invalid or missed
key_terms.يُفِيضُ: To depart or move from a place, specifically referring to leaving Arafat for Muzdalifah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who misses the standing at Arafat during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar clarifies the critical distinction between missing the *time* of standing at Arafat versus missing the *act* itself, emphasizing that al-Mash'ar al-Haram serves as a valid substitute for Arafat if reached before sunrise. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the pilgrimage is not entirely void if the pilgrim catches the second pillar, though it necessitates making up the missed component as a separate Umrah and repeating the Hajj the following year, reflecting the principle of divine ease (*al-'azr*) for the servant.
